text:
anya: Heads up — we got several customer tickets about p95/p99 spikes for text-gen and embedding APIs starting ~15:10 UTC. Customers report long queue delays and some 429s. :warning:
sam: Got the summary, can you paste an example request id / customer tenant?
anya: Example tenant: acme-inc, request id=req_0a9f3. Error logs show admission rejections and long wait times.
marco: Seeing ingress alerts too: queue length jump at 15:11. Pasting raw snippet from ingress logs:
```
2026-03-17T15:11:58Z ingress info queue_len=12 avg_wait_ms=120
2026-03-17T15:12:03Z ingress warn queue_len=820 admit_rejected=128 pool=gpu-pool-3
2026-03-17T15:12:10Z worker warn active_long_runs=42 pool=gpu-pool-3
2026-03-17T15:12:30Z ingress info queue_len=600 avg_wait_ms=900
```
jon: alerts-bot posted a surge event and tenant throttles fired: `tenants/ACME throttle=SOFT` at 15:12.
alerts-bot: [ALERT] ingress_queue_spike service=ingress region=us-west count=14 spike_start=2026-03-17T15:10:57Z
sam: Any config changes/deploys around then?
marco: No infra deploys. Product webhook shows a sudden bump of large prompt sizes + streaming calls from acme-inc starting 15:09. The requests were keeping KV cache warm and holding GPU for ~3-4s each which amplified queueing.
anya: Repro steps from support (shortened):
1) curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"rwd-2b","input":"<very long prompt>"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
2) Observe 202 or 429 after ~1s and then 5-6s latency on success
sam: Tried reproducing on staging with a 200rps burst and saw queue_len climb then backlog at admission layer. Snapshot from admit controller: `max_inflight=500, inflight=780, admit_pending=320`.
marco: Immediate mitigation suggestions:
- Route acme-inc to warm pool (gpu-pool-warm) to reduce cold waits
- Temporarily lower tenant soft concurrency cap to 20
- Increase admission controller short window token bucket by 2x for 10 minutes
sam: I pushed a canary change to routing to divert 5% of acme traffic to warm pool (deployed at 15:22). Also decreased tenant soft cap via admin UI (15:23).
anya: Support updated affected customers at 15:25 — apologised and said we were applying mitigations.
marco: After the routing change queue_len dropped to ~40 within ~90s. p99 for affected endpoints went from ~4.6s -> ~320ms.
jon: Do we have a root cause? Looks like a tenant-level misconfiguration causing too many large streaming requests simultaneously.
marco: Root cause: acme-inc switched to concurrent-calls=8k in their SDK config, combined with large prompt sizes and streaming enabled. That produced many long-held GPU sessions and blocked fair scheduling.
sam: Actions taken / next steps:
- Hotfix: tenant-level hard cap enforcement (implemented 15:40) -> will reject beyond cap with clearer 429 body and telemetry
- Short-term: improved admission bucket and warm-pool routing (done)
- Long-term: implement per-tenant windows + queue-prioritization, better alerting on average duration per tenant
- Follow-up: product to reach out to acme for SDK config guidance and rate limits
anya: Customer-facing note drafted, flagging that behavior is not typical and we recommend per-call concurrency <= 50 for streaming with rwd-2b.
marco: Logging/observability actions: add per-tenant avg-hold-time metric + a heatmap for queue wait distribution (assigned to eng-platform).
jon: Any remaining errors? I see a handful of replays but no active surge now. Last 30m p99 within normal bounds.
anya: Closing customer tickets with timeline and remediation steps.
sam: Will open a follow-up ticket to track the hard cap rollout and a playbook for rapid routing to warm pools.
marco: Note for postmortem: this was a tenant-driven long-tail holding problem, not an allocator bug. Recommend we ship clearer SDK defaults and fail-open vs fail-closed guidance.
anya: Thanks team — keep an eye on acme tenant for 24h and watch for any regressions. :thumbsup:
